clue.text: This makes one score century!

parts.note: multiplying by five is the process that turns a score, twenty, into a century, a hundred

explanation.surface: A cricket-flavoured boast about something that lets a batter reach a hundred runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' and 'century' look like cricket, but they are the numbers twenty and a hundred; the operation linking them is multiplying by five.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiplying by five turns twenty into a hundred, so the process described is fivefold multiplication.

clue.text: Almost time to charge Enterprise steersman's drive

indicators.note: to charge something is to load it, so the shortened time is loaded into the steersman's name

parts.note: Sulu is the helmsman of the starship Enterprise in Star Trek; with the possessive this gives SULUS

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: time taken as written before shortening

explanation.surface: A Star Trek scene: nearly time to power up the helmsman's engine drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter of TIME to give TIM, and 'to charge' loads TIM into SULUS (Sulu's).
explanation.definitionFit: A drive in the sense of an incentive or spur is a synonym for the answer.

clue.text: Anti-Gaelic lines?

parts.note: V stands for versus, meaning against
Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Scotland and Ireland

explanation.surface: Political slogans or poetry hostile to the Gaelic language.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry is made up of lines, so lines of poetry make up a stanza or poem.

clue.text: Syllabus lacking university permit stays

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the university letter is removed

parts.note: a syllabus is a course of study
to permit is to let

explanation.surface: A course of study with no university connection allows people to stay on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for a stiffened undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays are a boned undergarment; a light corset of that kind is the answer.

clue.text: Debtor? Send back into custody!

parts.note: a debtor is someone in the red, so a man placed inside the word red pictures one

explanation.surface: An exasperated creditor wants the person who owes money locked up again.
explanation.walkthrough: A debtor is 'in the red': put MAN inside RED and you get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that sends an accused back to jail to await trial is doing exactly this.

clue.text: See 21
Wine shop old alumnus set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: old means aged
an alumnus is an old boy, OB

explanation.surface: A former student established a wine shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' reverses AGED + OB in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spain a bodega is a wine cellar or shop selling wine.

clue.text: Idle heathen punished with this feature in the press

indicators.note: punished letters are knocked about and beaten into a new shape

explanation.surface: A lazy pagan, when punished, makes the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punished' rearranges IDLE HEATHEN together with THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To feature prominently in newspapers is the idiom for making big news.

clue.text: Mad as Saint Simeon?

definitions.meaning: British slang for crazy or deranged
Simeon Stylites lived for decades on top of a pillar, so he was literally aloft on a column

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for crazy, and literally describes being perched on a post or pillar.

clue.text: Mother-in-law your compiler grumbles about

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the phrase is written backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, I
to grumble is to moan

explanation.surface: The setter complains about their mother-in-law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reverses I MOAN. In the Book of Ruth, Naomi is Ruth's mother-in-law.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Ruth stays loyal to her husband's mother, the woman named here.

clue.text: Meissen gets smashed in retribution

indicators.note: smashed porcelain lies in pieces, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Fine Meissen porcelain is broken as an act of revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of vengeance, and her name now means deserved punishment.

clue.text: Surrounding compass points brought in

indicators.note: brought in means the points are placed inside the scope word

parts.note: compass in the sense of range or scope is an ambit
E and N are compass points, east and north

explanation.surface: Points on a compass have been brought into the surrounding area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compass points' looks like one phrase, but compass here means scope or range; 'brought in' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient means of the immediate surroundings, as in ambient temperature or noise.

clue.text: Wrecked guy snorts line? Not a pretty sight!

indicators.note: snorting takes something in, so the rearranged guy takes in the line letter
wrecked means ruined, so the letters of guy are broken up

explanation.surface: A drunk man snorting a line of cocaine is an unpleasant spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snorts' puts L inside UGY, the anagram of GUY from 'Wrecked'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unattractive or unpleasant to look at is no pretty sight.

clue.text: Horse saddle disintegrated in cold washing solution

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: in means the rearranged saddle sits inside the washing solution

parts.note: lye is an alkaline solution used for washing

indicators.note: disintegrated means falling to pieces, so the letters of saddle are rearranged

explanation.surface: A saddle falls apart after soaking in cold cleaning fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disintegrated' gives DESDAL, and 'in' sets it inside the alkaline washing liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A Clydesdale is a heavy Scottish draught breed, a kind of horse.

clue.text: Mistress, Indy's Teresa, shortly put in prison

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the prison word

parts.note: can is slang for prison
the setter writes for the Independent, nicknamed the Indy, so its things are ours

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter of the pet name goes

parts.note: Tess is a familiar form of the name Teresa

explanation.surface: A newspaper's own Teresa is briefly jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Indy is the Independent's nickname, so the setter's paper's things are ours; 'shortly' trims the pet name and 'put in' jails the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesan is a kept woman or high-class lover of wealthy men, a mistress.

clue.text: Fail to benefit thug drinking Holsten regularly

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so the thug swallows the chosen letters

parts.note: a lout is a thug

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the beer brand is taken

explanation.surface: A yob downing Holsten lager gets nothing out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' picks O, S, E from Holsten, which 'drinking' places inside LOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss out on an advantage is the phrasal verb meaning failing to gain.

clue.text: Criminal in store's looting

indicators.note: in means the criminal word is placed inside the store word

parts.note: a pile is a stock or store of things
lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A criminal inside a shop is out to steal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like an adjective, but it is LAG, put 'in' PILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Plundering and looting are synonyms, usually of a captured town.

clue.text: Fix medal over lapel centrally in sport

parts.note: to fix is to pin

indicators.note: the medal covers over the central lapel letter, so it sits round it

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal

indicators.note: centrally means the middle letter of lapel is taken

explanation.surface: Pinning a medal to the middle of a lapel at a sports ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centrally' gives P from lapel, which GONG goes 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: Table tennis is a sport, and this is its informal name.

clue.text: Graduate stops Mad Hatter getting drink?

indicators.note: stops means the graduate plugs a gap inside the rearranged letters
mad means the letters of Hatter are crazily rearranged

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree holder

explanation.surface: A graduate interrupts Alice's Mad Hatter while he gets a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' gives ATTHER, which the graduate 'stops'. The definition is playful: someone ordering at the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ordering a drink is standing at the pub counter, so the phrase fits jokingly.

clue.text: Get gull to circle one sitting on chicken

indicators.note: to circle is to surround, so the hoax word goes round the rest

parts.note: to gull someone is to cod them, both meaning to hoax
an MP is a Member of Parliament, one who sits in the House
re means on, concerning
a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: A seagull circles a person perched on a chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gull' is a verb here, to hoax, not the seabird; 'to circle' wraps it round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a point is to understand it, a synonym.

clue.text: Girl inducted by frantic bacchante

indicators.note: inducted by means taken inside the frantic word

parts.note: frantic means mad
Ena is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman is admitted into the society of a wild reveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inducted by' places the girl's name inside the frantic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Maenads were frenzied female followers of Bacchus, also called bacchantes.

clue.text: Hunt Ball set used to create much activity?

indicators.note: to create means the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A set of tableware used at a hunt ball to generate a busy scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To create' rearranges all of HUNT BALL SET USED; a hunt ball is a formal dance held by a fox-hunting club.
explanation.definitionFit: Busy commotion and bustle is what the phrase describes, an idiom.

clue.text: Maybe service centre one's pressed to close

definitions.meaning: a breeding farm where stallions serve mares
a press fastener that snaps shut

explanation.definitionFit: A breeding establishment for horses and a press fastener both carry this name.

clue.text: Small portion without starter's more than enough

indicators.note: without starter means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a sample is a small portion

explanation.surface: A tiny helping, with no first course, is more than enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without starter' drops S from SAMPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Plentiful or abundant, providing more than is needed.

clue.text: Greek hero recognised in Florida and Georgia?

parts.note: both states lie in the south-east of America

explanation.surface: A classical hero is spotted in two American states.
explanation.walkthrough: Florida and Georgia are found in THE SE (south-east) US.
explanation.definitionFit: The slayer of the Minotaur is a hero of Athenian legend.

clue.text: Round mass in pipe irked one? Smoker here blew top!

indicators.note: in means the round and mass letters are placed inside the rearranged pipe
irked means put out, so the letters of pipe are disturbed

parts.note: O is round in shape
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pipe smoker loses their temper and blows their top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irked' rearranges PIPE as PPEI, with OM put 'in'. The 'Smoker' is Vesuvius, whose eruption buried this town.
explanation.definitionFit: Vesuvius, the smoking volcano, erupted over this Roman town in AD 79.

clue.text: Asian city — it's in pretty good area

indicators.note: in means the it word goes inside the pretty good word

parts.note: OK means fair to middling, pretty good
it, as in sex appeal, is SA

explanation.surface: Sex appeal is to be found in an attractive neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is a crossword convention for sex appeal, SA.
explanation.definitionFit: A major port in Japan, so a city on that continent.

clue.text: Wartime agreement gives tennis coach freedom

parts.note: Ivan Lendl, former champion, coached Andy Murray
ease means freedom from difficulty

explanation.surface: A tennis coach grants a player liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivan Lendl was a tennis champion who later coached Andy Murray.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1941 US scheme supplying arms to Allies was a wartime pact of this name.
